conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, this is Revenue Officer Carter, badge ID 714329. Who am I speaking with today?
Hi, um, this is Emily Parker. I got a message saying I needed to call about my taxes?
Yes, Ms. Parker. I have your file open. This call concerns unresolved discrepancies in your 2021 and 2022 federal tax filings.
I just graduated last year, so I only filed taxes once. Is something wrong?
According to our audit, there are serious errors in your reported income, and a case for tax fraud has been initiated. I am required to inform you that there is now a federal warrant for your arrest.
Wait, what? A warrant? I don't understand, I've never done anything wrong!
Ms. Parker, this is a serious federal offense. If this is not resolved immediately, local law enforcement will be dispatched to your address within the hour.
Oh my God, no, please. I didn't mean to make any mistakes. What can I do?
Listen closely. The IRS allows a one-time rapid resolution for first-time offenders. If you settle the outstanding balance right now, we can cancel the warrant and avoid asset seizure.
Okay, what do I have to do? How much is it?
Your total owed, including penalties and legal fees, is $3,228. Payment must be made immediately. Are you able to make this payment in full right now?
I don't have that much in my bank account. I just started working. Is there any way I can pay part now?
Partial payment is acceptable today to stop the arrest process, but you must follow my instructions exactly. Do you have access to any credit cards or digital payment apps like Zelle or Venmo?
I use Venmo, but my credit card is almost maxed. I could pay maybe $900 right now.

That will suffice as an initial settlement. You must now send the $900 to the IRS rapid processing account via Venmo. I'll provide the IRS payment handler: send to @IRS-Remit-Dept and confirm once sent.
Wait, is that really the IRS? It looks like a regular Venmo username.
The IRS uses secure third-party payment handlers for urgent cases. This is the authorized account. If you delay, the system will auto-confirm your location for law enforcement.
Okay, okay, I'm sending $900 to @IRS-Remit-Dept now. Should I screenshot it?
Yes, screenshot your confirmation and read me the transaction ID to verify your payment and cancel the warrant.
Alright, the transaction ID is 9832457. Screenshot sent.

Received. That stops the legal action for now, but you must pay the remaining $2,328 within the next two hours. You can use prepaid Target or Best Buy gift cards for the balance. Do you have a store nearby?
There's a Target close to me. I guess I can go there.
Purchase four gift cards of $500 each and one of $328. Do not tell store staff this is for the IRS, or your case may escalate. Call me back as soon as you have the cards.
Okay, I'll go now. Should I stay on the line?
Stay on with me. Once you have the cards, scratch off the back and read me the codes. I will process your payment and issue your clearance letter.
